cabezon.notes: Verify current season dates and limits with WDFW.

blue-rockfish.notes: Blue rockfish are among the most common nearshore rockfish. Part of aggregate bag limit. Verify current WDFW regulations.

monkeyface-prickleback.notes: Pacific staghorn sculpin are common pier catch throughout the Pacific Coast. Excellent bait for halibut. Verify current WDFW regulations.

striped-bass-west-coast.notes: Striped bass are in the Columbia River system and some coastal areas. Verify current WDFW rules.

chinook-salmon.bag_limit: 2 per day (varies by area and season)
chinook-salmon.season: Set annually by PFMC; varies greatly by area and month
chinook-salmon.notes: WA salmon rules are extremely complex and change by year, area, and week. ALWAYS verify current WDFW Emergency Rules before fishing.

coho-salmon.notes: Verify current WDFW rules; coho seasons and quotas change frequently.

california-sheephead.notes: California sheephead do not occur in WA waters — CA-endemic species.

jack-mackerel.notes: Pacific jack mackerel rare in WA; possible during El Niño. No specific regulation.

pacific-barracuda.notes: Pacific barracuda are a Southern California species and do not occur in WA waters.

ulua-giant-trevally.notes: Ulua (GT) have no statewide bag limit but some areas may have restrictions.

papio.notes: Papio (juvenile ulua/GT) have no bag limit in Hawaii. Strong fighters on light tackle.

oio-bonefish.notes: Oio (bonefish) regulations; most anglers practice catch and release.

moi.notes: Moi (Pacific threadfin) have special cultural significance in Hawaii. Historically a royal fish (kapu), moi are now partially protected: fishing for moi at certain traditional fishponds and nearshore areas may be restricted. Check HI DLNR for current area-specific rules before targeting moi. Size and bag limits may apply in some zones.

permit.notes: Permit are found in Hawaiian flats. No specific bag limit.

great-barracuda.notes: Great barracuda (kaku) are common in Hawaii. No bag limit. Use caution with large fish (ciguatera risk in some areas).

bonefish.notes: Oio (bonefish) regulations; most anglers practice catch and release.

omilu-bluefin-trevally.notes: Omilu (bluefin trevally) have no specific bag or size limit in Hawaii. Excellent eating.

aholehole.notes: Aholehole (Hawaiian flagtail) are small but numerous shore fish. No bag limit. Good bait fish.

weke-goatfish.notes: No size or bag restrictions in Hawaii for recreational fishing.

akule.notes: No state bag or size limit for akule (bigeye scad) in Hawaii. Cast net and sabiki rig fishing allowed.

toau.notes: No size or bag restrictions. Salt water license not required in Hawaii for recreational fishing.

uku.bag_limit: No state bag limit for uku specifically
uku.notes: Verify current DLNR rules for any area restrictions.

kaku-barracuda.notes: Great barracuda (kaku) are common in Hawaii. No bag limit. Use caution with large fish (ciguatera risk in some areas).

nenue.notes: No state size or bag limit for nenue (Hawaiian chub) in Hawaii.

manini.notes: No state size or bag limit for manini (convict tang) in Hawaii.

amaama-mullet.notes: Striped mullet (amaama) are a traditional Hawaiian food fish. No bag limit.

mu.notes: Mu (bigeye emperor) are found on shallow Hawaiian reefs. No bag limit.

roi.bag_limit: No bag limit; anglers are encouraged to keep all
roi.notes: Roi is an invasive species introduced in 1956. DLNR encourages unlimited harvest to help control populations. No license required.

bluefish.notes: Bluefish appear in New Hampshire coastal waters and offshore from July through October. No minimum size; 10/day bag limit follows federal guidelines. Verify with NH Fish & Game.

speckled-trout.notes: Spotted seatrout are rare strays in NH. Stocks are not managed here — release all.

atlantic-croaker.notes: Atlantic croaker extremely rare in NH. May stray in warm years.

flounder.season: Seasonal — check NH Fish & Game for open dates
flounder.notes: New Hampshire follows ASMFC-aligned summer flounder limits. Minimum size and bag limit set annually — verify 2026 rules with NH Fish & Game before fishing.

spanish-mackerel.notes: Spanish mackerel are rare strays in NH waters. Primarily encountered during warm water years.

striped-bass.season: Seasonal (check NH Fish & Game for dates)
striped-bass.notes: New Hampshire follows ASMFC coastwide striped bass rules: 28-inch minimum, 1/day. A slot limit (28–35 in) may apply — verify 2026 rules with NH Fish & Game before fishing.

tautog.notes: New Hampshire follows New England tautog regulations: 16-inch minimum, 3/day. Seasonal closures typically in winter and summer. Verify current 2026 season dates with NH Fish & Game.

black-sea-bass.notes: Black sea bass at the northern edge of their range in NH. Follow ASMFC/NOAA regulations.

weakfish-gray-trout.notes: Weakfish occasionally appear in NH estuaries. Stocks are severely depleted; 1/day limit applies.

scup-porgy.notes: Scup appear in New Hampshire coastal waters in summer. 9-inch minimum, 30/day. Verify with NH Fish & Game.

winter-flounder.season: Apr 1 – Jun 30 (spring season); check NH Fish & Game
winter-flounder.notes: Winter flounder stocks are depleted; confirm current season and bag limits with NH Fish & Game.

atlantic-mackerel.notes: Atlantic mackerel caught from piers and boats in NH summer.

atlantic-bonito.notes: Atlantic bonito in NH offshore and nearshore in summer. No bag limit.

american-eel.notes: American eel in NH estuaries. Recreational fishing for personal use.

smooth-dogfish.notes: Smooth dogfish in NH coastal waters. No specific bag limit.

spiny-dogfish.notes: Spiny dogfish common in NH offshore and nearshore waters.

cobia.notes: Cobia are occasional warm-water strays in NH. Follow ASMFC regulations.

striped-bass-west-coast.season: Seasonal (check NH Fish & Game for dates)
striped-bass-west-coast.notes: New Hampshire follows ASMFC coastwide striped bass rules: 28-inch minimum, 1/day. A slot limit (28–35 in) may apply — verify 2026 rules with NH Fish & Game before fishing.

red-drum.notes: Red drum are rare in PA waters; primarily a lower Delaware Bay species.

bluefish.notes: Bluefish in lower Delaware River/Bay. Follow ASMFC federal bag limits.

speckled-trout.notes: Spotted seatrout occasionally enter Delaware Bay. Very rare north of Delaware.

atlantic-croaker.notes: Atlantic croaker reach lower Delaware Bay in fall.

sheepshead.notes: Sheepshead found around structure in Delaware River/Bay.

flounder.notes: Summer flounder in lower Delaware River. PA follows ASMFC regulations; verify current size limit.

spanish-mackerel.notes: Spanish mackerel are rare but possible in lower Delaware Bay during summer.

striped-bass.season: Seasonal (typically spring/fall); check PA Fish & Boat Commission
striped-bass.notes: Striped bass in Delaware River/Bay. PA follows Delaware River Basin Commission (DRBC) and PRFC rules.

tautog.notes: Pennsylvania anglers fishing Delaware River/Bay estuary may encounter tautog. 16-inch minimum, 3/day. Verify with PA Fish & Boat Commission and DE DNREC for tidal water rules.

black-sea-bass.notes: Black sea bass at southern Delaware Bay nearshore reefs. Verify current regulations with PA Fish & Boat Commission.

scup-porgy.notes: Scup present in Delaware Bay/River in warmer months. Federal bag limit applies.

winter-flounder.season: Seasonal — verify with PA Fish & Boat Commission
winter-flounder.notes: Winter flounder occasionally enter Delaware Bay from NJ/DE. Very rare in PA waters.

atlantic-mackerel.notes: Atlantic mackerel may be caught in lower Delaware Bay during their migrations.

spiny-dogfish.notes: Spiny dogfish in Delaware Bay and offshore PA waters. Follow NOAA regulations.
spiny-dogfish.source: PA Fish & Boat Commission; NOAA Fisheries

cobia.notes: Cobia are occasional strays in Delaware Bay. Very uncommon in PA waters.

king-mackerel.notes: King mackerel extremely rare in PA — far out of normal range.

striped-bass-west-coast.season: Seasonal (typically spring/fall); check PA Fish & Boat Commission
striped-bass-west-coast.notes: Striped bass in Delaware River/Bay. PA follows Delaware River Basin Commission (DRBC) and PRFC rules.

black-sea-bass.notes: Black sea bass do not occur in AK waters.

corbina.notes: Corbina are a Southern California species and do not occur in AK waters.

black-rockfish.notes: Alaska nearshore rockfish (including black rockfish): 5-fish aggregate daily limit. Found around kelp beds, rocky reefs, and piers. Some deep-water species (yelloweye, canary) have much lower limits. Verify area-specific rules with AK F&G.

lingcod.notes: Alaska lingcod: 35-inch TL minimum (stricter than most lower-48 states), 2/day bag limit. Found in shallow rocky reefs and kelp in Southeast and Southcentral Alaska. Check AK F&G for any area-specific closures.

starry-flounder.notes: Starry flounder in nearshore and estuary areas. Check current CDFW/ODFW/WDFW rules. Verify current ADF&G regulations.

kelp-greenling.notes: Kelp greenling common throughout AK nearshore waters. Follow ADF&G regulations.

cabezon.notes: Cabezon present in Southeast AK. Follow ADF&G saltwater regulations.

blue-rockfish.notes: Blue rockfish are among the most common nearshore rockfish. Part of aggregate bag limit. Verify current ADF&G regulations.

copper-rockfish.notes: Copper rockfish in SE AK. Included in rockfish aggregate bag limit.

monkeyface-prickleback.notes: Pacific staghorn sculpin are common pier catch throughout the Pacific Coast. Excellent bait for halibut. Verify current ADF&G regulations.

chinook-salmon.min_size: 20 in FL minimum in most areas
chinook-salmon.bag_limit: 1 per day (most areas); 0 in some closed systems
chinook-salmon.season: Seasonal — varies significantly by area; check AK F&G Sport Fishing Regulations
chinook-salmon.notes: Alaska king (chinook) salmon regulations are among the most complex in the world. Limits, minimum sizes, and seasons vary dramatically by drainage, area, and even specific sections of river. Some systems are closed entirely to king salmon fishing to protect wild stocks. Always check AK F&G current emergency order closures and area-specific rules before targeting king salmon. 20-in FL general minimum in saltwater; many freshwater systems differ.

coho-salmon.season: Seasonal — August through November in most areas; check AK F&G
coho-salmon.notes: Alaska coho (silver) salmon: generally 6/day in most saltwater and freshwater areas. Season typically August–November. Some systems restrict to hatchery-marked fish only. Check AK F&G for area-specific rules and emergency orders — regulations change annually.

pacific-barracuda.notes: Pacific barracuda are a Southern California species and do not occur in AK waters.
